navier_fit: Zero-emission foiling aligns with Costa Rica's carbon-neutral brand; resort density gives premium-charter anchor demand; Quanta-LR unlocks the long Pacific-coast legs.
regulatory_note: MarViva / SINAC marine-protected zones in the Gulf of Papagayo; clean propulsion eases permitting.
seasonality: Dry season Dec-Apr peak; Papagayo winds strongest Dec-Mar — a foiling hull's stability is an advantage in chop.
summary: The Gulf of Papagayo anchors Costa Rica's highest-end Pacific resort cluster (Four Seasons, Andaz, Marina Papagayo) just north of Liberia's international airport, while the broader Nicoya Peninsula is reached across the Gulf of Nicoya by a busy car-ferry system (Puntarenas <-> Paquera/Naranjo). Demand splits cleanly into luxury resort transfers and yacht movements in the north, and utilitarian peninsula access in the south where the land route is a long detour. Costa Rica's national zero-carbon brand makes a silent electric-foiling layer not just operationally attractive but a marketing asset for the destination. Pioneer II handles resort and gulf-crossing legs; Quanta-LR opens longer Pacific runs toward the Papagayo-to-Quepos/Manuel Antonio coast.
tagline: Costa Rica's Pacific luxury-resort coast and the Gulf of Nicoya ferry system — eco-credentials and resort density that fit a zero-emission foiling fleet like a glove.
